title.analysis: Authentic title "How People Treat You Once You Hit $1,000,000 Invested" promises a social-treatment payoff. The script argues the opposite: strangers do not change, family treats you worse if you tell, and only work and self-perception change. The promise is answered, but by contradicting its implied premise.

thumbnail.analysis: Registered maxresdefault 1280x720 (HTTP 200, real image). White split panels. Left "$900": the recurring cartoon man ignored by a faceless figure walking away. Right "$1M": the man in a tuxedo on a red carpet with a bowing figure and camera flashes. At 320x180 both figures and the "$900/$1M" labels read clearly. The thumbnail shows exactly the red-carpet treatment the script says does not happen; a clickbait contrast.

script.opening_words: You're standing in a Costco checkout line on a Tuesday afternoon and there are two guys ahead of you. Same age, 52, same khaki shorts. One of them just stepped out of a leased BMW X5 with a $1,140 monthly payment, a wrapped Apple Watch in his cart. The other one drove here in a 2016 Ford F-150 with 140,000 miles and a door dent he never bothered to fix. One of these men has 1.2 million dollars in index
script.ending_words: buy them without checking anything first. That's it. That's the whole prize. If you enjoyed this one, you'll probably like my video on every financial trap you'll face as your net worth grows. It's right up here. And let me know in the comments if you hit a million tomorrow, who's the first person you'd tell or would you tell no one? I read everything. Thanks for being here. Peace.
script.analysis: Full 20150 canonical characters read. A single-narrator essay with two composites (Costco BMW vs F-150, Dave the accountant): rarity of $1M, inflation of the millionaire image, Schwab and Ameriprise perception surveys, Munger and the climb, Ramsey millionaire profile, logo experiments and stealth signals, lottery myth correction, family requests and tall poppy, stealth wealth, walk-away money and the 4% rule, Piff experiments with replication caveat, wealth-sorted friendships, Killingsworth on happiness, a faceless-YouTube promotion and a close. Well-sourced overall; the Fidelity count is stale.
beat_map: Hook: two men at Costco; which is the millionaire?
Work: walk-away money and the 4% rule.
Self: Piff experiments; loneliness; Nature friendships.
